package.title: What If Your Twin Left at the Speed of Light?
alt_titles: Your Twin Came Home 45 Years Younger Than You
You're 75. Your Twin Is 30. This Is Real Physics.
description: Your twin leaves at 99.5% of the speed of light. Ten years pass on Earth for every one on their ship.
The math: at 99.5% c the Lorentz factor is about 10. Five years on their clock is fifty down here: they land at 30, you're 75.

The real part: in 1977, muons in CERN's storage ring moving at about 99.94% of light speed lived 29.3 times longer than muons at rest, just as relativity predicts. Scott Kelly's almost-a-year on the ISS left him a few thousandths of a second younger than he'd otherwise be, relative to his twin Mark.
Would you wave goodbye? Tell me in the comments.
sources: Bailey J. et al. (1977), Measurements of relativistic time dilatation for positive and negative muons in a circular orbit. Nature 268: 301–305. https://www.nature.com/articles/268301a0
package.pinned: Would you wave goodbye, knowing they'd come home the same age as your kids?
